title: CORS wildcard origin reflection with credentials enabled on all backend routes
description: The Express backend reflects any arbitrary Origin header value verbatim in Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Tested across /auth/me, /rbac/roles, /users, /health, /auth/token — all reflect attacker-controlled origins. Null origin is also reflected, enabling sandboxed iframe attacks.
evidence_safe: OPTIONS preflight to /auth/me with Origin: evil.attacker.com returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: [reflected origin] and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
evidence_quarantined:
access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.attacker.com
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-methods: GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,OPTIONS
access-control-allow-headers: Content-Type,Authorization

title: CORS wildcard reflection with credentials on unauthenticated /health endpoint (GET confirmed)
description: The GET request to /health with an attacker-controlled Origin returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflecting the attacker origin plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This endpoint is publicly accessible, so no victim authentication is needed to exploit CORS on this specific route.
evidence_safe: GET /health with attacker Origin returns 200 with reflected ACAO header and credentials: true. Response body includes status and env fields.
evidence_quarantined:
HTTP/2 200
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.attacker.com
body: {"status":"ok","env":"production"}

title: CORS null origin reflected with credentials: true — enables sandboxed iframe attacks
description: Sending Origin: null to the backend returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows attackers using sandboxed iframes (which send null origin) to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the backend.
evidence_safe: GET /health with Origin: null returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
evidence_quarantined:
access-control-allow-origin: null
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-methods: GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,OPTIONS

title: Unauthenticated /api/health endpoint leaks PostgreSQL version, OS, and compiler fingerprint
description: The Next.js /api/health endpoint returns detailed database and environment information without any authentication. The response includes PostgreSQL exact version with build hash, OS architecture (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu), GCC compiler version, and deployment environment names. This information aids in targeted exploitation.
evidence_safe: GET /api/health (no auth) returns 200 with database.connected:true, PostgreSQL major/minor version, build hash, OS platform, and GCC compiler version

title: Production domain /api/health also leaks database fingerprint without auth
description: The production domain revops.copointdata.com exposes the same /api/health endpoint without authentication, returning identical PostgreSQL version information. This confirms the vulnerability exists in the production environment, not just dev.
evidence_safe: GET /api/health on production domain (no auth) returns 200 with same PostgreSQL 17.8 version and OS fingerprint as dev environment

title: Backend /health endpoint accessible without auth — leaks environment name
description: The Express backend exposes a /health endpoint without authentication that returns a JSON body including the environment name (production). The response also leaks the X-Powered-By: Express header, confirming the framework.
evidence_safe: GET /health returns HTTP 200 with {status: ok, env: production} and X-Powered-By: Express header — no auth required

title: Express backend route surface enumerated — 50+ routes discovered behind global auth middleware
description: Comprehensive enumeration confirmed 50+ Express routes that return 401 (route exists, auth required). Routes span: auth, users, admin, rbac, accounts, contacts, deals, pipelines, graphql, docs/swagger, webhooks, integrations, audit, billing, and internal paths. All paths are protected by a global auth middleware returning consistent 401 JSON error.
evidence_safe: 50+ distinct URL paths return HTTP 401 with consistent JSON error body, confirming Express route existence with global auth middleware. Includes /rbac, /admin, /graphql, /users, /auth/* paths.

title: NextAuth provider configuration disclosed without auth — Azure AD OAuth details exposed
description: The /api/auth/providers endpoint returns the full Azure AD OAuth configuration without authentication, including the sign-in URL, callback URL, provider type, and provider ID. This confirms Azure AD as the identity provider and discloses OIDC callback endpoints.
evidence_safe: GET /api/auth/providers returns 200 with azure-ad provider ID, type oauth, signinUrl and callbackUrl for the application — no auth required

title: Pusher auth endpoint confirmed at /api/pusher/auth — redirects to login (auth required)
description: POST requests to /api/pusher/auth with socket_id and channel_name parameters return HTTP 307 redirect to /login, confirming the endpoint exists and Pusher real-time WebSocket functionality is implemented. Auth is required to use Pusher private channels.
evidence_safe: POST /api/pusher/auth with socket_id and channel_name params returns HTTP 307 redirect to /login, confirming endpoint existence and authentication requirement

title: pay.copointdata.com subdomain discovered — potential payment portal (currently unreachable)
description: Subfinder enumeration discovered pay.copointdata.com and www.pay.copointdata.com. The subdomain timed out during active probing, suggesting it may be behind a firewall, offline, or on an internal network. The pay. naming convention suggests a payment portal or billing interface.
evidence_safe: Subfinder returned pay.copointdata.com and www.pay.copointdata.com as valid subdomains. HTTP probe timed out — subdomain exists in DNS but service unreachable.

title: accelerate.copointdata.com subdomain discovered — purpose unknown, unreachable
description: Subfinder discovered accelerate.copointdata.com. The subdomain timed out during active HTTP probing. The accelerate. naming may suggest a CDN, performance tier, or separate product feature.
evidence_safe: Subfinder returned accelerate.copointdata.com as a valid subdomain. HTTP probe timed out — DNS entry exists but service unreachable.
